name: ggwave
summary: Audio modem toolkit for short-range data transmission over sound in air-gapped or network-limited environments.
why_it_matters: GGWave captures a distinct audio-transfer capability, but there is no current validated scenario that makes it worth maintaining as a supported resource.
when_to_use: A future scenario needs audio-based local data transfer or signaling.
Operators want air-gapped pairing or provisioning flows.
The workflow benefits from short text or token transfer over sound.

platform_support.notes: The underlying library is portable, but practical support depends on host audio device access and latency characteristics.

prerequisites: Audio input and output device strategy
Defined encode/decode workflow and message constraints
Validated signal quality expectations in target environments
implementation_notes: Future promotion should support one or two real pairing or transfer workflows.
Treat device access and protocol design as first-class concerns.
Avoid claiming production-grade reliability without environment testing.
operational_notes: Ambient noise and host audio routing materially affect behavior.
Validation should include a real encode/decode round trip.
Latency and payload-size expectations need to stay explicit.
risks: Novel capabilities are easy to keep speculatively without real demand.
Audio-device behavior differs enough by host to make support uneven.
